STEP 1 - Scene: A small side-style salad plate with steamed/boiled cauliflower florets and a bed of fresh arugula (rocket) with thin apple or pear slices, dressed lightly. Looks like a light lunch side or starter.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square-ish plate, roughly 22 cm across (side-plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Cauliflower florets (boiled/steamed, yellow, possibly turmeric-seasoned)
- Arugula/rocket leaves, lightly dressed
- Apple or pear slices (thin wedges)
- A small amount of dressing/oil sheen (not clearly visible in quantity)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Cauliflower: ~22% of vessel (≈84 cm²)
- Arugula: ~14% (≈53 cm²)
- Apple/pear slices: ~3% (≈11 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 39% (sum consistent with the visible plate area).

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Cauliflower: 84 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 210 ml
- Arugula: 53 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 133 ml
- Apple: 11 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 16 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Cauliflower: 210 ml x 0.7 ≈ 147 g (cooked, dense florets)
- Arugula: 133 ml x 0.15 ≈ 20 g
- Apple: 16 ml x 0.6 ≈ 10 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Cauliflower, cooked: 147 g x 23 kcal/100 g ≈ 34 kcal
- Arugula: 20 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 5 kcal
- Apple: 10 g x 52 kcal/100 g ≈ 5 kcal
Total ≈ 44 kcal (before dressing; a light oil dressing of ~5 g would add ~44 kcal, so I include a modest allowance).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 177 g of food, which is plausible for a side salad portion covering about 40% of a side plate. Energy is low, consistent with mostly vegetables. Dressing is uncertain, so the estimate carries a range of roughly 50–90 kcal.
